newsitem.title: USA: Mason-Dixon should weigh merger, says group.
newsitem.headline: Mason-Dixon should weigh merger, says group.

text.p: A group which owns a 5.1 percent stake in Mason-Dixon Bancshares Inc said Friday the company should explore opportunities for a merger or consolidation or similar deals.

The group, led by Anthony Investments Inc, a Saverna Park, Md., firm, said it suggested this step to Mason-Dixon after it found in a review, among other things, that the bankholding company's earnings were below industry level.
The group said it will make a proposal embodying its stand at Mason-Dixon's next annual meeting, if the company itself does not include the issue in its proxy statement.

It said it will also consider other steps such as getting in touch with other shareholders, talking to institutions interested in proposing an acquisition deal or nominating people that will support its position.
The group said that, of the 268,671 shares of Mason-Dixon that it holds, it bought 24,640 shares between October 24 and November 13 at prices ranging from $17.25 to $20.75 a share.
Mason-Dixon is parent of Carroll County Bank and Trust Co and operates retail banking offices in Maryland.
